body_html:
There are many ways to say thank you in Spanish, and choosing the right one shows you understand the moment. Gracias works everywhere, but a quick favor, a generous gift and a formal email each call for something a little different. Mil gracias sounds warm and casual, te lo agradezco mucho sounds sincere and personal, and le agradezco su atención belongs in a professional message. Here are the phrases I use most, grouped by situation, along with the best ways to answer.

Quick answer
  • Everyday: Gracias. Muchas gracias. Mil gracias.
  • Sincere: Te lo agradezco mucho. No sabes cuánto te lo agradezco.
  • Formal: Le agradezco su ayuda. Muchas gracias por su atención.
  • Replies: De nada. Con gusto. No hay de qué.
{{toc}}

Everyday ways to say thank you in Spanish

SpanishEnglish
Gracias.Thanks.
Muchas gracias.Thank you very much.
Muchísimas gracias.Thank you so much.
Mil gracias.A thousand thanks. (warm, casual)
Gracias por todo.Thanks for everything.
Gracias por tu ayuda.Thanks for your help.
¡Qué amable!How kind of you!
Eres un amor.You’re a sweetheart.

Notice gracias por: thanks always takes por, never para, because you are giving thanks in exchange for something. See {{link:por-vs-para|por vs para}}.

Sincere, heartfelt thanks

When someone has really helped you, agradecer (to thank, to be grateful for) sounds more personal than gracias alone:

  • Te lo agradezco mucho. I really appreciate it.
  • No sabes cuánto te lo agradezco. You have no idea how grateful I am.
  • Te debo una. I owe you one.
  • No tengo cómo agradecerte. I don’t know how to thank you.
  • Gracias de corazón. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
  • Estoy muy agradecido. I’m very grateful. (agradecida if you are female)
{{image:2}}

Formal thanks for work and emails

In professional settings and with people you address as usted, use these:

  • Le agradezco su ayuda. Thank you for your help.
  • Muchas gracias por su atención. Thank you for your attention. (end of an email or presentation)
  • Le agradezco de antemano. Thank you in advance.
  • Agradecemos su preferencia. Thank you for choosing us. (businesses to customers)
  • Quedo muy agradecido por la oportunidad. I’m very grateful for the opportunity. (after an interview)

For full email templates, see {{link:writing-emails-in-spanish|writing emails in Spanish}} and {{link:job-interview-in-spanish|job interview in Spanish}}.

How to reply to thank you

SpanishEnglish
De nada.You’re welcome.
Con gusto.My pleasure. (very common in Mexico and Colombia)
No hay de qué.Don’t mention it.
Para eso estamos.That’s what we’re here for.
A ti.Thank you. (returning the thanks)
A usted.Thank you. (formal, returning the thanks)
No fue nada.It was nothing.
Cuando quieras.Anytime.

A ti and a usted are what you say when the thanks should go both ways: a cashier thanks you for shopping, and you answer Gracias a usted.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Thanking for gifts, meals and hospitality

Some moments have their own phrases:

  • A gift: ¡Qué detalle! Muchas gracias. What a thoughtful gift! Thank you so much. No te hubieras molestado. You shouldn’t have.
  • A meal: Gracias por la comida, todo estuvo delicioso. Thanks for the meal, everything was delicious.
  • Hospitality: Gracias por recibirme en su casa. Thank you for having me in your home.
  • A compliment: Gracias, qué amable. Thank you, that’s kind of you.
  • Good wishes: Gracias, igualmente. Thanks, same to you.

¡Qué detalle! is one of the nicest phrases to know. A detalle is a small, thoughtful gesture, and naming it shows you noticed the care behind it.

Gracias across the Spanish-speaking world

The basic words are the same everywhere, but habits differ. In Mexico and Colombia, con gusto is a very common reply, and people thank each other often, even for small things. In Spain, de nada is the standard reply, and very close friends sometimes skip “thank you” altogether because it can feel too formal between them. In Argentina you may hear de nada, che or simply nada. Whatever you hear, a warm gracias is never wrong.

{{image:3}}

Thanking in real situations

Vecina: Le traje unos tamales que me sobraron.
I brought you some tamales I had left over.

Tú: ¡Ay, qué amable! Muchísimas gracias, se ven deliciosos.
Oh, how kind! Thank you so much, they look delicious.

Vecina: No hay de qué. Para eso estamos los vecinos.
Don’t mention it. That’s what neighbors are for.

Tú: Se lo agradezco de verdad. La próxima vez le invito yo.
I really appreciate it. Next time it’s on me.

This kind of exchange is everyday life in many neighborhoods; see {{link:talking-to-neighbors-in-spanish|talking to neighbors in Spanish}}.

Common mistakes

  • Gracias para todo. Use por: Gracias por todo.
  • Te agradezco a ti. Redundant; just say Te lo agradezco.
  • Muy gracias. Gracias is a noun here, so it takes muchas: Muchas gracias. See {{link:muy-vs-mucho|muy vs mucho}}.
  • Estoy agradecido para tu ayuda. Use por: Estoy agradecido por tu ayuda.

The RAE dictionary entry for agradecer shows how the verb is used with an object: you thank someone for something by making that thing the object, as in te agradezco la ayuda.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Knowing several ways to say thank you in Spanish lets you match your words to the moment: gracias for small things, te lo agradezco for real help, le agradezco at work, and con gusto when it’s your turn to reply. For more everyday moments, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: What are the most common ways to say thank you in Spanish?
faq.a: Gracias, muchas gracias, mil gracias and te lo agradezco.

faq.q: How do you say thank you formally in Spanish?
faq.a: Use le agradezco or muchas gracias por su atención, with usted forms.

faq.q: What is the difference between “de nada” and “con gusto”?
faq.a: Both mean “you’re welcome”. Con gusto (“with pleasure”) sounds a little warmer and is very common in Mexico and Colombia.

questions.explain: Muy gracias is incorrect; use muchas gracias.
